subject: Invoice sweep pilot & dynamic net-term trial
content:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mark Eaton <mark.eaton@solarahealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Invoice sweep pilot & dynamic net-term trial

Mark —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, we wanted to put a short written proposal on the table for a limited pilot that helps both teams:

Proposal (8-week pilot) — high level:
- \"Invoice sweep\" mechanism: Redwood will perform a weekly cash-sweep against outstanding invoices up to an agreed weekly cap. Sweeps are applied only to invoices older than 14 days.
- Dynamic net-term trial: For invoices captured by the sweep we propose moving those invoices to Net30 for the duration of the pilot in exchange for a 1.5% per-invoice discount. Other invoices remain on your negotiated Net45 schedule.
- Credit cap: initial cap at $75k/week aggregate sweep, with a temporary credit corridor of $250k (total outstanding threshold before we pause the sweep).
- VAT & tax handling: Redwood will supply full VAT-compliant invoice copies and a weekly VAT summary per legal entity to simplify Solara’s reclaim process; for EU entities we’ll add a reverse-charge reference where applicable.

Attached: sample invoice extract and a short spec of the sweep mechanism (sweep-mechanism-spec.xlsx).

We want the pilot to be low-friction: no direct debit from your operating account — Redwood will create a weekly remittance file and your treasury can approve/decline the sweep batch (we’ll accept a scheduled auto-approve after the first two successful weeks). If this sounds reasonable I can loop in Marissa on the amendment language and we can route a DocuSign.

If you need us to side-step the sweep and instead do a partial prepayment schedule vs. credit-limit increase, we can sketch that too.

Goal: validate whether a targeted cash-sweep + Net30 discount materially reduces your supplier float without disrupting Solara’s internal planning.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
(attachment: 2026-05-20-solara-invoice-sample.pdf)

---

From: Mark Eaton <mark.eaton@solarahealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice sweep pilot & dynamic net-term trial

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear write-up. A few quick items from treasury before we greenlight a pilot:

1) VAT: we need Redwood invoices to explicitly state VAT registration for Redwood’s EU entities and include the reverse-charge note where applicable. Our reclaim team will need the ledger-friendly CSV (one you mentioned) and a signed statement clarifying who is the supplier of record for each legal entity.
2) Auto-approve: treasury is wary of any automatic debit. We can approve weekly remittance batches for a pilot but only after we see two consecutive clean weeks where sweep totals reconcile with our AR system.
3) Cap: $75k/week sounds like a reasonable starting point. If cashflow needs change we’ll ask to pause — please confirm a quickest-path pause mechanism (ideally a single email to finance@redwoodinference.com that pauses the next scheduled sweep).
4) Contract: any change in payment terms for invoices must be covered by an amendment that references the original SOW and the discount per-invoice. We’ll need procurement and legal (cc’d) to sign.

Finally — since you mentioned a discount for Net30 — can you confirm whether the discount applies per invoice flagged for the sweep or per remittance batch? That determines our internal allocation treatment.

If you can get Marissa the draft amendment and the VAT statement, I’ll circulate to procurement and legal.

—Mark Eaton
CFO, Solara Health
(External: finance team copied to finance@solarahealth.com)

---

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mark Eaton <mark.eaton@solarahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice sweep pilot & dynamic net-term trial

Team —

Per Mark’s notes above, quick internal asks so we can respond with concrete docs:
- Marissa: can you draft a short 8-week amendment (attachment: amendment-draft.docx) that covers the discount mechanics, weekly cap, and the pause/unpause flow (single email to finance@redwoodinference.com to pause)?
- Lauren: can you confirm the operational pause path in Console (how we surface the scheduled sweep file and what permission toggles are needed)? If treasury wants a manual approve step we need to ensure a human can approve the batch before submit.
- Vivek: please confirm whether our finance/legal teams are ok adding a reverse-charge reference line to EU invoices (I believe this is fine if the service is B2B, but we should confirm which Redwood legal entity is the supplier of record).

Operational note: for accounting treat the discount as an early-payment credit applied to the related invoice (so it stays visible on the invoice-level accounting entry). Mark’s question on per-invoice vs per-batch: we should apply discount per invoice captured by the sweep — cleaner for his allocator.

I’m attaching the sweep spec for your reference.

Jordan

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice sweep pilot & dynamic net-term trial

Jordan / team —

Draft amendment notes (high level):
- Pilot length: 8 weeks, per-invoice 1.5% discount applied at time of sweep. Discount appears as a credit line item on each invoice.
- Weekly cap: $75,000 sweep max; aggregate outstanding threshold (pause trigger) $250,000.
- Pause clause: Solara may pause by emailing finance@redwoodinference.com with 48 hours notice before the next scheduled sweep. Redwood may pause if thresholds are exceeded or for suspected reconciliation failures.
- VAT: we will include Redwood legal entity VAT numbers on all invoices and add a standard reverse-charge note for B2B EU transactions. We will also produce a weekly CSV ledger for Solara that includes invoice id, gross, VAT, net, reverse-charge flag, and remittance amount.
- Credit increase: to enable smoother sweep, recommend temporary credit corridor increase to $350k (internal approval required). If approved we can uplift the aggregate threshold from $250k to $350k which reduces the chance of mid-week pauses.

I’ve attached the amendment draft (amendment-draft.docx). Question for Jordan: do we want the discount to be taxable (i.e., reduce taxable base) or show as a separate non-taxable credit? Tax prefers reducing the taxable amount, but legal might prefer separate line items. If Solara needs a specific treatment for VAT reclaim, call it out and we’ll adapt.

Marissa Cole
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
(attachment: amendment-draft.docx)

---

From: Mark Eaton <mark.eaton@solarahealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice sweep pilot & dynamic net-term trial

Jordan / Marissa —

Thanks — this is helpful. Procurement and legal have reviewed the short amendment and are comfortable with the terms as written, contingent on the VAT statement and the CSV ledger format matching our AP ingestion spec. Two confirmations before we sign: 

1) Discount tax treatment: Solara prefers the discount to reduce the taxable base (cleaner for reclaim). If Redwood can reduce the taxable amount on the invoice that will make our treasury and tax teams happiest.
2) Pause path: the 48-hour notice to pause is acceptable. We’d like the first two weeks to be manual-approve only; after that treasury will allow auto-approve for the pilot if reconciliations are clean.

With those two confirmations Solara is ready to run the 8-week pilot starting the week of June 7th. We’ll sign the amendment once we receive the VAT statement and the CSV template. Please send a DocuSign link for the amendment when ready.

Mark Eaton
CFO, Solara Health
(attachment: none)

---

[Thread summary / action items]
- Redwood: update amendment to reflect discount reduces taxable base; attach VAT registration statement and sample CSV. (owner: Marissa)
- Redwood Ops: surface manual-approve toggle in Console and document the pause email flow. (owner: Lauren)
- Redwood Credit: escalate temporary credit corridor to $350k internal approval; otherwise proceed with $250k aggregate threshold. (owner: Vivek)
- Solara: sign amendment via DocuSign once VAT statement + CSV are provided; pilot target start date week of 2026-06-07.

(attachments referenced: 2026-05-20-solara-invoice-sample.pdf, sweep-mechanism-spec.xlsx, amendment-draft.docx)
